US-119-HJRES221.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States giving Congress power to regulate campaign contributions for Federal elections.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HJRES221.aiSummary: The resolution would propose a constitutional amendment giving Congress power to set rules on campaign contributions and spending in federal elections. It would also let states set similar rules for state elections, while requiring those rules to be applied the same way to all citizens and citizen groups. It would bar noncitizens, foreign governments, and their agents from giving money or using it to affect elections in the United States.

US-119-S5638.title: Protecting American Workers Through H–1B Modernization Act.

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5638.description: A bill to amend the Immigration and Nationality Act to modernize the wage required for exempt H-1B workers, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5638.aiSummary: The bill would change the wage rule for certain exempt H-1B workers in the Immigration and Nationality Act. It would replace the current $60,000 minimum with a wage set at two times the national average wage index for the most recent year. This would affect H-1B workers and the employers who use that visa category.

US-119-S4406.title: Next-Generation Geothermal Research and Development Act

actions.text: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Ordered to be reported without amendment favorably.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S4406.description: A bill to amend the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to direct research, development, demonstration, and commercial application activities in support of next-generation geothermal systems in various conditions, and for other purposes.
US-119-S4406.aiSummary: The bill would update federal geothermal energy rules to support research, testing, and commercial use of next-generation geothermal systems, including enhanced and closed-loop systems. It would add new definitions, expand data sharing and mapping for geothermal projects, and call for deeper drilling data and public data updates. It would also create grant programs, a center of excellence, and a report on water use, and it would require at least one FORGE site to be able to test next-generation geothermal systems in supercritical conditions within 1 year after enactment.

US-119-HCONRES119.title: Celebrating the 65th anniversary of the establishment of the Peace Corps, and commending its volunteers and contributions to global peace, friendship, and development.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
Submitted in House

US-119-HCONRES119.aiSummary: This concurrent resolution would celebrate the 65th anniversary of the Peace Corps and honor its volunteers. It would recognize their work in global peace, friendship, and community development. The measure affects the Peace Corps and the people who have served in it.

US-119-S1513.title: Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe Project Lands Restoration Act
US-119-S1513.summary:
Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe Project Lands Restoration Act

This bill takes approximately 1,082.63 acres of specified lands in Washington into trust for the benefit of the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe. Land taken into trust shall be part of the tribe's reservation.

Further, the bill prohibits gaming on the land taken into trust.

US-119-S4901.title: Preventing Crimes Against Veterans Act of 2026
US-119-S4901.summary:
Preventing Crimes Against Veterans Act of 2026

This bill establishes a new federal criminal offense for knowingly executing, or attempting to execute, a scheme to defraud an individual of veterans' benefits, or in connection with obtaining veteran's benefits for an individual. A violator is subject to criminal penalties—a fine, a prison term of up to five years, or both.
US-119-S4901.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in Senate, 2026-06-24)

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S4901.aiSummary: The bill would make it a federal crime to knowingly carry out, or try to carry out, a plan to cheat someone out of veterans' benefits, or to do so when getting benefits for a veteran. A person who breaks this rule could face a fine, up to five years in prison, or both.

US-119-HR2616.title: Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act
US-119-HR2616.summary:
Parental Rights Over The Education and Care of Their Kids Act or the PROTECT Kids Act

This bill requires public elementary and middle schools, as a condition of receiving certain federal funds for elementary and secondary education, to obtain parental consent before changing a student's gender on school forms or changing a student's sex-based accommodations.

Specifically, an elementary school or a school consisting of only grades 5-8 must obtain parental consent before changing a minor student's (1) gender markers, pronouns, or preferred name on any school form; or (2) sex-based accommodations, including locker rooms or bathrooms.
